title: The thinkers, looking back
tomorrow: John is told 'lion.' he turns to look. what does he see?

lines: RESTLESS, UNTIL IT REPOSE IN THEE.
cards: Two in the morning, phone in hand, scrolling for something with no name.

Augustine wrote about that kind of restlessness, straight to God, near the start of his Confessions: “Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.” That's where it rests.
Now a very different voice. John Mbiti, an African scholar, summed up one idea he found in African religion and life roughly like this: I am, because we are.

teach.b: Between those two lines runs a long conversation. Augustine thinks by praying out loud; his Confessions is written to God, as Thou.
Anselm, an archbishop writing in Latin, gave the conversation a motto: faith seeking understanding. Faith that keeps asking because it cares. Mbiti widens the table.
Put his line beside Augustine's, and something rhymes: the restless heart isn't meant to rest alone. Christians still argue with all three, and that's how a conversation stays alive.
Paul had already said why nobody gets the last word: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.”
Every thinker wrote from this side of that glass, so nobody finished the thought.
Each one passed it on, the way this week did: a plowboy promise, a cloud of runners, a turning year, a creed said together, many rooms of prayer, and love at the center.

how: Some Christians read thinkers like Augustine, Anselm and Mbiti in study groups, seminaries or on their own, often a few pages at a time alongside the Bible.

o: the leaders who ran churches through the centuries
Christian thinkers in one long conversation about God
the writers of the Gospels and nobody else

games.q: the week, looking back — tap the pairs.
p: restless until it rests in Thee

s: Augustine's Confessions is a memoir written to its readers
it's written to God, as Thou: thinking and praying side by side.
Anselm's motto is faith seeking understanding
fides quaerens intellectum: faith that keeps asking because it cares.
Christian thinkers all agree with one another
they argue, refine and disagree; that's the long conversation.

games.q: your little brother says asking hard questions about God means you don't really have faith. what does Anselm's motto say?
o: questions mean faith is already gone.
faith seeking understanding: faith asks because it cares.
only scholars are allowed to ask questions like that.
games.why: for Anselm, asking isn't the opposite of faith; it's faith at work. Augustine prays his restlessness straight to God.

practice: Walk slowly for about a minute, around a room or down a hallway, carrying one line: our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee, or I am, because we are. Then sit for the bell and let the line keep you company.
If you pray, end where Augustine does, speaking to God as Thou.
